lba_qa.q: Two roads cross each other. One of the four angles formed at the crossing is 70 degrees. Find the angle exactly opposite to it and explain why.
lba_qa.a:
When two lines cross, the angle opposite (vertically opposite) angles are EQUAL.

Given one angle = 70 degrees.

The angle exactly opposite to it:
= 70 degrees (vertically opposite angles are equal) ✅

Reason: Vertically opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are always equal.

lba_qa.q: A straight road has a signboard pole. Two angles on one side of the road add up along the straight line. If one angle is 110 degrees, find the other.
lba_qa.a:
Angles on a straight line form a LINEAR PAIR and add up to 180 degrees.

Given one angle = 110 degrees.

Other angle = 180 - 110
= 70 degrees ✅

Reason: The sum of angles on a straight line (linear pair) is always 180 degrees.

lba_qa.q: Two angles are complementary. One angle is 35 degrees. Find the other, and give a real example of complementary angles.
lba_qa.a:
Complementary angles ADD UP to 90 degrees.

Given one angle = 35 degrees.

Other angle = 90 - 35
= 55 degrees ✅

Real example: The corner of a book is 90 degrees. If a pencil is placed making 35 degrees with one edge, it makes 55 degrees with the other edge.

lba_qa.q: A ladder leans against a wall. The angle between the ladder and the ground is 65 degrees. The wall is vertical (90 degrees to ground). Find the angle between the ladder and the wall.
lba_qa.a:
The ground and the wall meet at 90 degrees.

The ladder makes 65 degrees with the ground.
The three angles at the foot region: the angle with the ground + angle with the wall = 90 degrees (since wall is vertical).

Angle between ladder and wall:
= 90 - 65
= 25 degrees ✅

So the ladder makes a 25 degree angle with the wall.

lba_qa.q: A railway track has two parallel rails cut by a sleeper (transversal). If one angle made is 120 degrees, find its co-interior (allied) angle.
lba_qa.a:
When a transversal cuts two parallel lines, co-interior (allied) angles ADD UP to 180 degrees.

Given one angle = 120 degrees.

Co-interior angle = 180 - 120
= 60 degrees ✅

Reason: Co-interior angles on the same side of the transversal between parallel lines are supplementary (sum 180 degrees).

lba_qa.q: Two parallel walls are crossed by a slanting beam. One angle made by the beam with the first wall is 50 degrees. Find the corresponding angle at the second wall.
lba_qa.a:
When a transversal cuts parallel lines, CORRESPONDING angles are EQUAL.

Given angle at first wall = 50 degrees.

Corresponding angle at second wall:
= 50 degrees ✅

Reason: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal with two parallel lines are always equal.

lba_qa.q: In a triangular roof truss, two angles are 55 degrees and 65 degrees. Find the third angle.
lba_qa.a:
The three angles of a triangle ADD UP to 180 degrees (angle sum property).

Given two angles = 55 degrees and 65 degrees.

Third angle = 180 - (55 + 65)
= 180 - 120
= 60 degrees ✅

So the third angle of the truss is 60 degrees.

lba_qa.q: At 3 o'clock, the hour hand and minute hand of a clock form an angle. Find that angle and explain.
lba_qa.a:
A clock face is a full circle = 360 degrees, with 12 hour marks.

Angle between two consecutive hour marks:
= 360 / 12
= 30 degrees

At 3 o'clock:
- Minute hand points at 12
- Hour hand points at 3
- They are 3 hour-marks apart

Angle = 3 x 30 = 90 degrees ✅

So the hands form a 90 degree (right) angle at 3 o'clock.

lba_qa.q: An exterior angle of a triangle is 110 degrees. One of the two opposite interior angles is 45 degrees. Find the other interior opposite angle.
lba_qa.a:
Exterior angle property: an exterior angle equals the SUM of the two opposite interior angles.

Given: exterior angle = 110 degrees, one interior opposite angle = 45 degrees.

So:
110 = 45 + other angle
Other angle = 110 - 45
= 65 degrees ✅

The other interior opposite angle is 65 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: Two straight roads cross. One angle at the crossing is 65 degrees. The vertically opposite angle is:
lba_mcq.explanation: Vertically opposite angles formed by two intersecting lines are equal, so it is also 65 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: On a straight line, one angle of a linear pair is 130 degrees. The other angle is:
lba_mcq.explanation: Angles in a linear pair add up to 180 degrees, so the other angle = 180 - 130 = 50 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: Two angles are complementary. If one is 40 degrees, the other is:
lba_mcq.explanation: Complementary angles add up to 90 degrees, so the other = 90 - 40 = 50 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: A transversal cuts two parallel rails. One corresponding angle is 75 degrees. The other corresponding angle is:
lba_mcq.explanation: Corresponding angles formed by a transversal with parallel lines are equal, so it is also 75 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: In a triangle, two angles are 70 degrees and 60 degrees. The third angle is:
lba_mcq.explanation: Angles of a triangle add to 180 degrees, so third angle = 180 - (70 + 60) = 50 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: At 6 o'clock, the angle between the hour and minute hands of a clock is:
lba_mcq.explanation: Each hour mark is 30 degrees apart. At 6 o'clock the hands are 6 marks apart: 6 x 30 = 180 degrees (a straight line).

lba_mcq.q: Co-interior (allied) angles between two parallel lines cut by a transversal always:
lba_mcq.explanation: Co-interior angles on the same side of the transversal between parallel lines are supplementary, adding up to 180 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: An exterior angle of a triangle equals 120 degrees. The sum of its two opposite interior angles is:
lba_mcq.explanation: The exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two opposite interior angles, so the sum is 120 degrees.

lba_mcq.q: Two angles are supplementary. If one is 115 degrees, the other is:
lba_mcq.explanation: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees, so the other = 180 - 115 = 65 degrees.
